title: Invoke surface adapter and schema-diff resolver for cross-SDK tool calls
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: Deliver a lightweight, language-idiomatic invoke surface adapter plus a runtime schema-diff resolver that makes tool/function calling robust across SDK versions and minor schema evolution. This ticket covers design + implementation across Python, TypeScript, and Go SDKs, including examples, tests, and rollout plan.

Motivation: Teams keep hitting interoperability bugs when model-prompts/third-party tool schemas change subtly (optional fields added/renamed, enum expansions). Current strict validation causes hard rejections for callers and forces brittle server-side coercions. We need an SDK-level layer that: 1) performs strict validation by default, 2) offers a configurable permissive mode that attempts safe coercions and emits diagnostics, and 3) stabilizes streaming invocation semantics for partial responses + resume.

Scope:
- Design an "Invoke Surface Adapter" API pattern per-language (decorator/middleware for Python/TS, context-wrapped invoker for Go) that encapsulates schema validation, coercion policy, idempotency keys, and retry hooks.
- Implement a schema-diff resolver that: (a) computes a minimal compatibility plan between caller schema and runtime tool schema, (b) applies safe coercions (type coercion for numeric/string, enum fallback maps, optional field defaulting), and (c) logs structured diagnostics (warning vs error).
- Streaming ergonomics: support chunked tool responses with resumable checkpoints and idempotent retry semantics. Provide a unified token/embed representation for resume so client can reattach to partial results without duplication.
- Examples: Python decorator example, TypeScript middleware factory, Go invoker wrapper. Include a small end-to-end sample that calls a toy "calendar.create_event" tool with evolving schema.
- Tests: unit + cross-sdk interop tests, simulation harness exercising schema evolution cases, perf microbench for validation overhead.
- Docs: short design doc, SDK API reference, migration guide for customers.

Non-goals: Rewriting server-side tool catalog or changing model-side contract enforcement. This is an SDK-side compatibility shim only.
acceptance_criteria: Cross-SDK invoke adapter implemented for Python/TS/Go and exposed via documented API
Schema-diff resolver produces deterministic plan and applies safe coercions in permissive mode
Streaming resume tokens allow reattach without duplicated side-effects in at-least-once retry scenarios
Automated interop test covers 6 schema-evolution scenarios and passes across all SDKs
Performance overhead for validation < 2ms per invocation in common fast-path (measured in microbench)
Design doc, usage examples, and migration notes published in docs repo
comments: 2026-02-15 Aisha Patel - Kickoff: Drafted initial design and compatibility rules. Posted design doc link to Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/SDK/Invoke+Adapter+and+Schema+Diff+Resolver. Set cross-SDK demo to use calendar.create_event toy tool.

2026-02-20 Marco Liu - Implementation plan: Python decorator + runtime hook for validator; TS middleware to plug into SDK client pipeline; Go wrapper using context and functional options. Starting with strict validator and a separate permissive coercion mode behind flag.

2026-02-27 Engineering sync: Agreed coercion rules: numeric<->string cast allowed in permissive mode, enums map by case-insensitive match and fallback to 'OTHER' only if server advertises default mapping; renames will be handled by heuristic map if field-level JSON path similarity > 0.7. Added telemetry events for every coercion applied.
2026-03-02 PR #7892 opened (Python): initial decorator, schema parser, and basic coercion rules. Link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/7892. PT: @marco for review.

2026-03-04 Code review notes: Reviewer requested explicit opt-in for permissive mode and stronger integration tests around streaming resume. Also requested that coercion warnings be accessible via a structured diagnostics API rather than only logs.

2026-03-06 Marco Liu - Addressed review: implemented Diagnostics object (list of diagnostic entries) returned when permissive mode used. Updated JSON-serializable diagnostics shape. Added unit tests for numeric->string coercion and enum fallback.

2026-03-08 Integration test harness: Ran interop harness between Python client and mock runtime with evolved schema (+optional 'location' field, enum expansion). Observed 0 functional failures in permissive mode but 3 strict rejections as expected. Performance microbench shows median +0.7ms overhead per invocation in Python.

2026-03-09 Security review note: Security flagged that permissive mode must never permit downcasting of numeric precision without explicit opt-in. Added a guard to reject float->int coercion unless caller sets 'allow_precision_loss'.

2026-03-10 QA: Streaming resume implemented for Python and TS; Go prototype in review. QA validated resume token by interrupting stream after 2 chunks and reattaching. Side-effect check: duplicate tool side-effects detected when server does not guarantee idempotency; added requirement to emit idempotency-key header and recommend server-side idempotency support.
